previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and alcohol withdrawal symptoms. He had been drinking heavily and presented with tremors and hallucinations consistent with delirium tremens. His pain was attributed to an acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis, despite a normal lipase. He also had mild alcoholic hepatitis with elevated AST and bilirubin, and an asthma exacerbation requiring albuterol nebulizers and a steroid burst. He was managed with CIWA protocol for withdrawal, IV fluids, pain control with hydromorphone, and respiratory support. His condition improved over five days—he stabilized, tolerated a regular diet, and had resolution of withdrawal symptoms. He was discharged home with pain medication, continued liver and asthma therapies, and referrals for alcohol rehabilitation and follow-up care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ male with PMHx alcoholic cirrhosis, alcohol abuse 
complicated by withdrawal seizures and recent admission to ___ 
for alcohol withdrawal, asthma with multiple intubations in the 
past presenting intoxicated with abdominal pain consistent with 
pancreatitis and shortness of breath consistent with asthma 
exacerbation. 

#Acute Pancreatitis: Patient with a history of recurrent 
pancreatitis and chronic alcohol use presented with worsening 
epigastric pain radiating posteriorly with lipase 160, 
suggestive of acute pancreatitis. RUQUS showed patent portal 
vein ruling out portal vein thrombosis. Patient was initially 
given IV dilaudid for pain. The patient was initially NPO and 
our plan was to slowly advance the diet once the patient was not 
requiring IV pain medications. On his second hospital day, he 
requested to stop IV pain medications and advance his diet but 
after eating he reported increased pain and wanted to go back on 
the IV medications. Ultimately he was weaned from IV dilaudid to 
PO dilaudid and then was discharged home on regular, low fat 
diet. While patient requested pain medications, but was advised 
to discuss further with his PCP. 

# EtOH Withdrawal/abuse: Patient presented acutely intoxicated 
with history of ETOH withdrawal seizures and DTs. A few days 
prior he was discharged from ___ where he was admitted for EtOH 
withdrawal and put on a phenobarbatol taper. Given that he had 
recently had phenobarb taper at ___, and seemed very symptomatic 
he was put on 5mg diazepam q8h standing in addition to 10mg 
diazepam q4h:prn for CIWA >10. He was also given thiamine 500mg 
IV x TID x 3 days, folate 1mg ___, a multivitamin. He was also 
restarted on his home acomprosate. Patient had no episodes of 
seizures or uncontrolled withdrawals.

# Asthma Exacerbation: Patient presented with acute SOB and 
wheezing on exam suggestive of likely in the setting of an acute 
asthma exacerbation. He was given duonebs and albuterol inhaler 
PRN as well as started on a 60mg daily prednisone burst on ___ 
with a plan for 5 day burst with significant improvement in 
sypmotms. 

# Opioid maintenance: Patient takes methadone as an outpatient 
(for substance abuse). Clinic was contacted and the dose was 
confirmed at 50mg/day and continued as an inpatient. 

#Iron Deficiency Anemia. Possible etiologies include poor iron 
intake vs. blood loss. Stool guiac was negative, but chronic GIB 
still a concern, especially in this patient with cirrhosis and a 
hx of gastritis. He was given IV ferrous sulfate while 
inpatient. 

#Thrombocytopenia. Platelet count 65-90k during this admission, 
likely due to worsening liver disease. Patient has scattered 
ecchymosis but no serious bleeding complications. He did not 
have any bleeding complications. 

#Tooth Ache: He complained of a tooth ache on his left upper 
molar. On exam he had  evidence of tooth decay on exam. We 
encouraged him to follow up with a dentist as an outpatient. 

Mr. ___ is a ___ male with PMHx of alcoholic 
cirrhosis, alcohol abuse complicated by withdrawal seizures and 
recent admission to ___ for alcohol withdrawal, asthma with 
multiple intubations in the past presenting intoxicated with 
abdominal pain consistent with pancreatitis and shortness of 
breath consistent with asthma exacerbation. Given chronic 
alcohol use with worsening epigastric pain that radiates 
posteriorly with lipase 160, concern was for acute pancreatitis, 
however repeat labs that were not hemolyzed showed a normal 
lipase. Right upper quadrant ultrasound showed patent portal 
vein without thrombosis. Patient was given IVF and made NPO and 
given dialudid for pain medication. Serum EtOH levels were 0.28 
and patient was placed on CIWA with diazepam. The patient had 
significant benzodiazepine requirements. Patient was also noted 
to be short of breath, raising concern for asthma exacerbation 
and started on steroid burst (Prednisone 60mg x5days). Breathing 
quickly improved. Patients signs/symptoms of alcohol withdrawal 
resolved and CIWA was discontinued. Patient was very hungry and 
diet was advanced. He was able to tolerate low fat diet. Patient 
was weaned from IV to PO dilaudid. Given ability to tolerate 
regular diet, no longer having alcohol withdrawal, and breathing 
comfortably on room air able to ambulate, deemed stable for 
discharge.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The liver is
enlarged but the contour of the liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass.
The right portal vein is were first but the left portal vein is forward and is

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD measures 2 mm.

without masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic
tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.

RETROPERITONEUM:  Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

Large liver without focal lesions.  Portal hypertension with a patent
umbilical vein.  Moderately enlarged spleen.  .
